title: CUCM Call Admission Control (CAC) Rejection Trending

dataSources: `sourcetype=cisco:ucm:syslog` (CAC events), `sourcetype=cisco:ucm:cdr` (cause code 47) Collected via Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: `Splunk Connect for Syslog`, `TA for Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics` (Splunkbase #4434) — Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352)
spl:
index=voip sourcetype="cisco:ucm:cdr" destCause_value=47
| eval location_pair=origNodeId." → ".destNodeId
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as cac_rejections by _time, location_pair
| eventstats avg(cac_rejections) as avg_rej, stdev(cac_rejections) as std_rej by location_pair
| eval z_score=round((cac_rejections - avg_rej)/nullif(std_rej, 0), 2)
| where cac_rejections > 5
| table _time, location_pair, cac_rejections, avg_rej, z_score
| sort -cac_rejections
description: Call Admission Control prevents WAN link saturation by rejecting calls when bandwidth allocation is exhausted for a location pair. CAC rejections mean users hear reorder tone or get rerouted to PSTN (higher cost). Trending CAC rejections by location directly supports SD-WAN, MPLS, and QoS capacity planning by quantifying where and when voice bandwidth demand exceeds allocation.
value: Early 'CUCM Call Admission Control (CAC) Rejection Trending' detection reduces operational risk and delayed incident response by giving Operations operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: CUCM CDR cause code 47 (Resource Unavailable) indicates CAC rejection. Map `origNodeId` and `destNodeId` to location names via a CUCM location lookup extracted from CUCM Admin. Trend rejections by hour and location pair to identify peak congestion windows. Correlate with WAN utilization data from SD-WAN (cat-05) to validate whether the location bandwidth configuration matches actual link capacity. Alert when any location pair exceeds 5 rejections in an hour — this indicates active user impact. Use this data to justify bandwidth upgrades or QoS policy changes. Track week-over-week trends to measure whether capacity additions reduce rejections.
visualization: Line chart (CAC rejections per location pair over 7 days), Heatmap (hour of day × location pair), Table (top rejected location pairs), Single value (total rejections today vs yesterday).
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable; primary SPL uses raw or vendor-normalized event fields.

Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: `Splunk Connect for Syslog`, `TA for Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics` (Splunkbase #4434).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype=cisco:ucm:syslog` (CAC events), `sourcetype=cisco:ucm:cdr` (cause code 47).
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
CUCM CDR cause code 47 (Resource Unavailable) indicates CAC rejection. Map `origNodeId` and `destNodeId` to location names via a CUCM location lookup extracted from CUCM Admin. Trend rejections by hour and location pair to identify peak congestion windows. Correlate with WAN utilization data from SD-WAN (cat-05) to validate whether the location bandwidth configuration matches actual link capacity. Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=voip sourcetype="cisco:ucm:cdr" destCause_value=47
| eval location_pair=origNodeId." → ".destNodeId
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as cac_rejections by _time, location_pair
| eventstats avg(cac_rejections) as avg_rej, stdev(cac_rejections) as std_rej by location_pair
| eval z_score=round((cac_rejections - avg_rej)/nullif(std_rej, 0), 2)
| where cac_rejections > 5
| table _time, location_pair, cac_rejections, avg_rej, z_score
| sort -cac_rejections
```

Understanding this SPL

**CUCM Call Admission Control (CAC) Rejection Trending** — Call Admission Control prevents WAN link saturation by rejecting calls when bandwidth allocation is exhausted for a location pair. CAC rejections mean users hear reorder tone or get rerouted to PSTN (higher cost). Trending CAC rejections by location directly supports SD-WAN, MPLS, and QoS capacity planning by quantifying where and when voice bandwidth demand exceeds allocation.

Documented **Data sources**: `sourcetype=cisco:ucm:syslog` (CAC events), `sourcetype=cisco:ucm:cdr` (cause code 47). **App/TA** (typical add-on context): `Splunk Connect for Syslog`, `TA for Cisco CDR Reporting and Analytics` (Splunkbase #4434). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: voip; **sourcetype**: cisco:ucm:cdr. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

• `eventstats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by location_pair** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **z_score** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare with CUCM RTMT, CallManager service parameters, and CDR/CMR or quality reports in Cisco unified communications admin for the same cluster and interval.

Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner.
